summary: We have developed a website that processes satellite wildfire and thermal hotspot datasets. This website can merge the data between two different satellites, MODIS and VIIRS, covering the period from 2015 to 2025. We faced a problem that the two satellites (MODIS and VIIRS) have different levels of accuracy. So, we made this website to do harmonization between the two datasets to make it easy for researchers to compare the data over the years in an accurate and useful way without conflicts, all in one place. This project is important because accurate monitoring of wildfires and climate changes supports faster decision-making, while understanding historical fire patterns (from 2015 to 2025) helps predict future risks and protect forests and the environment.
details: First, we collected historical hotspot data from the two satellites (MODIS and VIIRS) from 2015 to 2025. We processed and merged the data to unify the differences between them. After that, we uploaded all the data we collected and processed on the website so that the user can search by date, location, or fire intensity and the website displays the results. This saves users a lot of time and effort because instead of downloading huge files from two different sources and struggling to clean and merge them, our website provides ready, clean, and unified data in one place. Beyond saving time, our project aims to help scientists, researchers, and decision-makers accurately understand the patterns and history of wildfires and climate changes over 10 years, which helps in predicting future risks, speeding up disaster response, and protecting forests and the environment.To build this project, we used multiple tools and technologies. First, we collected the historical wildfire datasets (MODIS and VIIRS) from NASA Firms. For data analysis and processing, we used Python and its libraries (such as Pandas) on Google Colab to clean and harmonize millions of records. Finally, for web development, we used JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and SQL to build an interactive and user-friendly interface. Our project is creative because it solves the complex problem of sensor differences between MODIS and VIIRS over a 10-year period and presents millions of raw records in a simple, interactive web interface. Instead of dealing with complicated tables, users can easily explore and compare historical wildfire data seamlessly. While developing the project, our team considered three main factors: performance, to handle millions of historical records without slowing down the website; data accuracy, to ensure that the harmonization process preserves the true readings of each satellite without distortion; and user experience, by designing a clean and simple interface that makes searching fast and easy.
